newsitem.title: RUSSIA: SOCCER-RUSSIA PLANS TO REDUCE SIZE OF PREMIER LEAGUE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-RUSSIA PLANS TO REDUCE SIZE OF PREMIER LEAGUE.

text.p: Russian soccer authorities plan to reduce the premier league from 18 to 16 teams for the 1998 season to help the national squad prepare for the next World Cup, a soccer official said on Friday.

Vladimir Rodionov, general director of the Russian Soccer Union, said the move would reduce the number of fixtures and make it easier schedule a long break in Russia's championship in the run-up to the 1998 World Cup finals in France.
"We have taken a final decision to cut the number of teams to create better conditions both for the national side and clubs, especially just before World Cup '98," Rodionov told Reuters by telephone.
"We experienced difficulties in the past when compiling the soccer calender. Teams often play two matches a week and they complain about this."
Rodionov said three premier league teams would be relegated at the end of the coming season, which starts in March, and only one team would be promoted.
Until now, three teams have been promoted and three relegated each season. It has not yet been decided how many teams would be promoted and relegated at the end of the 1998 season, Rodionov said.

The Russian soccer authorities, trying to improve their teams' record in European competitions, have also debated playing through winter instead of summer to bring their season into line with Europe but recently rejected the idea.

The national team's record in recent years is also a cuase for concern. Russia have often promised much but failed to produce the goods when it mattered most, performing miserably at the last two World Cup finals and also at Euro '96 in England.
